pages.lesson:
LESSON: ADDITION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.2: Addition

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Addition. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can you estimate the sum of given numbers?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. add up to three 6-digit numbers without regrouping up to a sum not exceeding 1,, in different situations
2. add up to two 6-digit numbers with double regrouping with the sum not exceeding 1,, in different situations
3. estimate sum by rounding off the addends to the nearest hundred and thousand in different situations

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Addition.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Addition using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Creativity and imagination: learner makes number patterns involving addition.
2. Digital literacy: learner uses digital devices and other resources to learn and play games in addition concept development. Values:
3. Unity: learner collaborates with others to work out the sum of two 6-digit numbers.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you estimate the sum of given numbers?
2. How can you create patterns in addition?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Addition is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
